AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim as that section binds every batch. The sim has no add-to-room phase - creature creation IS construction - so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (fossil_stalker.py:36-40). Same observable today, established by execution rather than assumed, on all three clauses: (a) listener set - the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:26-40 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on target is self.player / applier is self.player / card is not None, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none of them can fire; sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks. (b) HP-roll inversion - the sim applies the power before the Niche roll and the game after it; of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp at all and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581), never at apply time. (c) roll ordering - MachineMonster.__init__ rolls the first move (state_machine.py:301) before the subclass applies its powers, but `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op: every initial state is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. RULE 7 NOTE: that rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does NOT hash, exactly as the seam records disclose. This unit's payload is PowerCmd.Apply<SuckPower>(..., Creature, 3m, Creature, null) (FossilStalker.cs:48) vs PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, SuckPower, 3) (fossil_stalker.py:40) - self-applied, amount 3 on both sides, no card. Nothing about it escapes the three clauses: SuckPower's amount is a literal, not a read of max_hp, and the initial state is the MoveState LATCH_MOVE, so clause (c)'s sticky no-op holds (executed: monster_probes_b03.py graphs shows initial=LATCH_MOVE, state_log=['LATCH_MOVE'], telegraph=LATCH_MOVE).

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: THIS IS THE SEAM'S COUNTER-EVIDENCE MONSTER AND IT HOLDS. FossilStalker.cs:58-60 calls AddBranch(LATCH,2), AddBranch(TACKLE,2), AddBranch(LASH,2) - overload #9 (`int maxRepeats`, RandomBranchState.cs:105), so each integer is maxRepeats 2, the weight defaults to 1f and the repeat type is forced to CanRepeatXTimes. The port reads all three correctly: fossil_stalker.py:57-59 passes repeat_type=CAN_REPEAT_X_TIMES, max_times=2 as KEYWORDS and leaves weight at its 1.0 default - it does NOT put the 2 in add_branch's positional slot 2, which is where monster_state_machine G1's five misreading ports put it. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py branch-args`): every branch reads {'weight': 1.0, 'repeat_type': CAN_REPEAT_X_TIMES, 'max_times': 2, 'cooldown': 0}. Branch ADD ORDER also matches (LATCH, TACKLE, LASH on both sides), which is observable because RandomBranchState.GetNextState resolves an equal-weight tie toward the earlier branch (monster_state_machine step 14). Graph: TACKLE/LATCH/LASH all follow up to the branch 'RAND' (FossilStalker.cs:57 assigns the same RandomBranchState to all three FollowUpStates), initial state LATCH_MOVE, states list [RAND, TACKLE, LATCH, LASH] in the same order as the C# List. Intents: SingleAttackIntent(9)+DebuffIntent -> ATTACK/DEBUFF, SingleAttackIntent(12) -> ATTACK 12, MultiAttackIntent(3,2) -> ATTACK 3x2.

guards.what: TackleMove applies Frail to `targets`, not to a fixed player
guards.rationale: FossilStalker.cs:74 PowerCmd.Apply<FrailPower>(ctx, targets, 1m, Creature, null) applies to the move's target list; fossil_stalker.py:66 applies to ctx.player. Identical in the Ironclad-only single-player sim, where the move's target list is exactly [player]. Multiplayer-only difference, noted in the mapping per PROMPT.md scope rather than verdicted as a divergence.

guards.what: Frail is applied AFTER the Tackle damage, on both sides
guards.rationale: FossilStalker.cs:70-74 awaits the Attack then applies Frail; fossil_stalker.py:63-66 does the same order. Ordering matters here because Frail is a block debuff and the attack is a monster attack, so a Frail applied first would not change this turn but WOULD change the block the player gains next turn relative to any block gained mid-move; both sides agree, so no PROMPT.md class-1 hook-order exposure.

All 29 PROMPT.md bug classes checked against this unit. Class 6 (AddBranch integers) is the headline and is CLEAN here, executed above. Class 10 (reset timing): the model holds no per-combat field at all. Class 21 (death is not removal): FossilStalker neither kills nor is retained. Class 24 (docstring misdescribes the port): fossil_stalker.py:28-30 says 'none more than twice in a row', which is exactly what CanRepeatXTimes(2) means (monster_state_machine step 19) - verified against the code, not the comment.
